title: Rotation scoping mismatch causing privilege escalation between orgs during token refresh
creator: Aisha Malik
description: Multiple customers reported unexpected cross-organization access following API key rotations and token refreshes in Dedicated and Private deployments. Investigation shows that under a rare combination of rolling rotations and scaled routing, the token refresh endpoint returned a session token scoped incorrectly (missing tenant binding), allowing a refreshed token to be used against a different org's resources. Hosted deployments are largely unaffected due to a separate auth proxy that enforces org headers; the issue appears in our self-hosted auth-service path used by Dedicated/Private customers. This ticket tracks the immediate remediation, root cause fix, test coverage, rollout, and customer communications.
reproducible_steps: 1) Use Dedicated/private deployment with API key rotation enabled and at least two auth-service replicas behind the router
2) Start a request using API key A from org-A, trigger an in-flight refresh (client calls /token/refresh) while rotation moves API key A to a new rotation epoch

3) Router routes the refresh to replica-1 which has stale local cache but global rotation metadata updated, replica-1 performs cache lookup missing tenant-scoped key and falls back to a global-apikey lookup

4) Replica-1 issues a new access token lacking org-specific claim (tenant_id) or with the wrong tenant_id, client receives token and then is able to call endpoints scoped to org-B (if routing sends them there), reproducing cross-org access
5) Observe auth-service logs that show cache_miss->global_lookup->issued_token without tenant_id and a concurrent rotation event within the same second
impact_summary: High severity. Two enterprise customers (AcmeHealth and FinDataCo) reported elevated privileges after key rotations; they were able to access resources from other org contexts for a short window. No evidence yet of data exfiltration, but immediate token/key rotation and audit required. Affects Dedicated and Private (on-prem) installations using auth-service v1.12.0->v1.13.4; Hosted uses a hardened proxy and shows no reproductions.
technical_root_cause: Auth-service cache key derivation omitted tenant_id under a fallback path when a local cache miss coincided with a rotation epoch change. The fallback used an unscoped key (global api_key_id) leading to tokens being minted without tenant binding. Additionally, there was a race in the in-memory rotation_epoch update path between replicas where a refresh request could observe a partially updated state.
fix_summary: 1) Scope the cache and token minting logic to require tenant_id + api_key_id + rotation_epoch in all lookup paths. 2) Add an atomic rotation_epoch update with versioned metadata to avoid partial reads. 3) Return explicit errors for refresh attempts that cannot be bound to a tenant instead of falling back to global lookup. 4) Add unit, integration, and e2e tests that simulate rotation+refresh races. 5) Backport patch to auth-service releases 1.13.x and 1.12.x and publish a dedicated hotfix image for self-hosted customers.
rollback_plan: If the fix causes regressions, rollback to auth-service v1.13.3 (or previous stable) using the existing deployment rollback scripts. For Dedicated customers, revoke the hotfix image and instruct clusters to revert using the same helm rollbacks. Notify customers via the incident channel before rollback.
rollout_plan: Cut auth-service v1.13.5-hotfix with cache key scoping changes
Deploy canary to 3 pods in staging and run replayed rotating+refresh traffic
Canary to 10% of production Dedicated clusters (non-critical) for 2 hours while monitoring auth_mismatch_rate and token_issuance_without_tenant metrics
If metrics stable, ramp to 100% across Dedicated, then publish hotfix image and helm chart for Private customers and coordinate with SRE/Customer Success for on-prem upgrades
Trigger forced rotation of affected API keys for high-risk customers and provide rotation script + audit logs
postmortem_actions: Add automated e2e test in CI that replays rotation+refresh race scenarios
Instrument a new metric: token_issued_without_tenant -> alert at >0
Update runbook sections for token rotation to include tenant-scoped verification step
Audit all Dedicated/Private clusters for auth-service versions and schedule mandatory hotfix upgrades
Customer notification template and assisted rotation script prepared by Customer Success
